title: Erdos #1166: Cumulative Most-Visited Points in Planar Random Walks

problemStatement.formal: For a planar random walk, prove |union_{k <= n} F(k)| <= (log n)^O(1) almost surely for all sufficiently large n, where F(k) is the set of most-visited points at time k.
problemStatement.plain: Does the cumulative set of sites that ever become most visited up to time n stay polylogarithmically small?
whyMatters: Links instantaneous favourite-site bounds with growth of the cumulative favourite-site set.
Combines the eventual smallness of F(n) with Erdos-Taylor control of the maximum visit count.
The Lean file contains substantial finite-set counting infrastructure around an axiomatized almost-sure random-walk layer.

proven: Lean defines RandomWalk, visitCount, maxVisitCount, mostVisitedSet, and cumulativeMostVisited.
The file proves monotonicity, maximum-achievement, most-visited nesting, cumulative containment, and finite-set cardinality bounds.
The polylog cumulative bound is derived from axiomatized eventual |F(n)| <= 3 and Erdos-Taylor maximum-visit-count ingredients.
open: The probability filter, eventual most-visited bound, and Erdos-Taylor constant theorem are active axioms.
RandomWalk.starts_at_origin is a structure field assumption in the model.
The file should not be described as a full formal construction of planar random-walk probability or a proof of Erdos-Taylor.
knownResults.goal: Show the internal proof architecture for the cumulative polylog bound while clearly marking the three deep probabilistic assumptions.

currentState.focus: Metadata now describes the visit-count/cumulative-set infrastructure and the derived polylog bound without overstating the axiomatized probability inputs.
blockers: asProbFilter, mostVisited_bounded_eventually, and erdosTaylor_constant remain axioms.
A full random-walk probability measure is not formalized.
currentState.nextAction: Future work can strengthen the random-walk probability model or reduce the Erdos-Revesz and Erdos-Taylor inputs to imported theorem interfaces.
